# Enums, types & console

<div class="gen-note">Generated from the APS 3.0 source code: every name, pin, default and description below is read from the plugin itself, so it matches what you see in the editor.</div>

The choices (enums) and data (structs) APS nodes and events pass around, with every value and field.

## Enums
### APSArchetype
<div class="comp-doc"><p>Ready-made starting points for the kinds of AI people build most.</p><p>These exist to prove the kernel is genre-blind as much as to save time: four very different AI over one unchanged core, each of them nothing but values on an ordinary profile.</p></div>
<div class="table"><table class="enum"><thead><tr><th>Value</th><th>Meaning</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr id="v-apsarchetype-guard" data-search="Guard" data-text="APSArchetype"><td><b>Guard</b></td><td></td></tr><tr id="v-apsarchetype-civilian" data-search="Civilian" data-text="APSArchetype"><td><b>Civilian</b></td><td></td></tr><tr id="v-apsarchetype-stalker" data-search="Stalker" data-text="APSArchetype"><td><b>Stalker</b></td><td></td></tr><tr id="v-apsarchetype-military-patrol" data-search="Military Patrol" data-text="APSArchetype"><td><b>Military Patrol</b></td><td></td></tr><tr id="v-apsarchetype-wildlife" data-search="Wildlife" data-text="APSArchetype"><td><b>Wildlife</b></td><td></td></tr></tbody></table></div>

### APSBelief Subject
<div class="comp-doc"><p>What a belief is *about*.</p><p>Until now a belief always pointed at an AActor, which meant the AI could only believe in things it could already name. &quot;Someone is in that room&quot;, &quot;a gunshot came from the bank&quot;, &quot;there is a body here&quot; had nowhere to live — and an anonymous stimulus had to be scored against whichever actor happened to be under evaluation, which is how one explosion made a guard suspicious of three unrelated bystanders at once.</p><p>Actor is the original case and still the default, so nothing that existed before behaves differently.</p></div>
<div class="table"><table class="enum"><thead><tr><th>Value</th><th>Meaning</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr id="v-apsbelief-subject-actor" data-search="Actor" data-text="APSBelief Subject"><td><b>Actor</b></td><td></td></tr><tr id="v-apsbelief-subject-location" data-search="Location" data-text="APSBelief Subject"><td><b>Location</b></td><td></td></tr><tr id="v-apsbelief-subject-descriptor" data-search="Descriptor" data-text="APSBelief Subject"><td><b>Descriptor</b></td><td></td></tr><tr id="v-apsbelief-subject-object" data-search="Object" data-text="APSBelief Subject"><td><b>Object</b></td><td></td></tr></tbody></table></div>

### APSComms Channel
<div class="comp-doc"><p>How a report reached the faction.</p><p>Squad sharing in the kernel is instant, lossless and range-gated, which makes every AI on a team effectively telepathic. These are the routes information actually travels by, each with its own cost — and the reason silencing a witness before they reach a radio is a real tactic rather than a cosmetic one.</p></div>
<div class="table"><table class="enum"><thead><tr><th>Value</th><th>Meaning</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr id="v-apscomms-channel-direct-witnessed" data-search="Direct (witnessed)" data-text="APSComms Channel"><td><b>Direct (witnessed)</b></td><td></td></tr><tr id="v-apscomms-channel-shout" data-search="Shout" data-text="APSComms Channel"><td><b>Shout</b></td><td></td></tr><tr id="v-apscomms-channel-radio" data-search="Radio" data-text="APSComms Channel"><td><b>Radio</b></td><td></td></tr><tr id="v-apscomms-channel-report-in-person" data-search="Report (in person)" data-text="APSComms Channel"><td><b>Report (in person)</b></td><td></td></tr></tbody></table></div>

### APSEye Direction Mode
<div class="comp-doc"><p>Where the vision cone&#x27;s DIRECTION comes from.</p><p>Epic&#x27;s AIPerception always uses the controller&#x27;s control rotation, which has no connection to the skeletal mesh — head turns, aim offsets and lean animations never move the cone. These modes let you bind facing to what the mesh is actually doing.</p></div>
<div class="table"><table class="enum"><thead><tr><th>Value</th><th>Meaning</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr id="v-apseye-direction-mode-actor-rotation" data-search="Actor Rotation" data-text="APSEye Direction Mode"><td><b>Actor Rotation</b></td><td></td></tr><tr id="v-apseye-direction-mode-control-rotation" data-search="Control Rotation" data-text="APSEye Direction Mode"><td><b>Control Rotation</b></td><td></td></tr><tr id="v-apseye-direction-mode-socket-rotation-head-bone" data-search="Socket Rotation (head bone)" data-text="APSEye Direction Mode"><td><b>Socket Rotation (head bone)</b></td><td></td></tr><tr id="v-apseye-direction-mode-blended-actor-socket" data-search="Blended (actor + socket)" data-text="APSEye Direction Mode"><td><b>Blended (actor + socket)</b></td><td></td></tr></tbody></table></div>

### APSEye Socket Alignment
<div class="comp-doc"><p>How the eye socket&#x27;s rotation is turned into a look direction.</p><p>A bone&#x27;s local axes are arbitrary — on Epic&#x27;s mannequin the head bone&#x27;s X axis runs UP the neck, so binding a vision cone straight to it aims the AI at the sky. Sockets can carry a corrective rotation, but only if whoever made them bothered to orient it.</p></div>
<div class="table"><table class="enum"><thead><tr><th>Value</th><th>Meaning</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr id="v-apseye-socket-alignment-automatic-recommended" data-search="Automatic (recommended)" data-text="APSEye Socket Alignment"><td><b>Automatic (recommended)</b></td><td></td></tr><tr id="v-apseye-socket-alignment-use-socket-rotation-as-authored" data-search="Use Socket Rotation As Authored" data-text="APSEye Socket Alignment"><td><b>Use Socket Rotation As Authored</b></td><td></td></tr><tr id="v-apseye-socket-alignment-manual-offset" data-search="Manual Offset" data-text="APSEye Socket Alignment"><td><b>Manual Offset</b></td><td></td></tr></tbody></table></div>

<div class="comp-doc"><p>Why a sense produced nothing this evaluation.</p><p>&quot;The AI can&#x27;t see me and I don&#x27;t know why&quot; is the single most common question a perception system gets asked. The pipeline already knows the answer at every early return — it just used to throw it away.</p></div>

### APSDescriptor
<div class="comp-doc"><p>A set of traits — either what somebody actually is, or what a witness managed to make out. The same type serves both, which is what lets one be matched against the other.</p></div>

### APSMemory Subject
<div class="comp-doc"><p>What a memory is about.</p><p>Any belief subject qualifies — a person, a place, an object. &quot;I remember something happened here&quot; is the same mechanism as &quot;I remember him&quot;, which is why this is a subject rather than an actor pointer.</p><p>Build one with Make Actor Subject or Make Place Subject.</p></div>

### APSPerception Frame
<div class="comp-doc"><p>One target&#x27;s belief at one moment, as recorded.</p><p>Perception bugs are temporal: the frame that explains the problem is always the one that has just gone past. A recording keeps the last few seconds so the interesting frame can be looked at after the fact instead of being chased with a breakpoint.</p><p>Deliberately small. This is written every tick for every tracked target, so a field that is merely interesting costs memory on every agent in the level.</p></div>

### APSProfile Override
<div class="comp-doc"><p>One changed number, named by property.</p><p>The composition system needs a way to say &quot;this profile, but with a longer vision range&quot; without duplicating an asset that has 170 fields on it. Where a child asset exists the difference can be read off the asset itself, but a per-agent tweak has no asset to diff against, so it is expressed as a list of these instead.</p><p>Property is the exact name as it appears on the profile, e.g. &quot;VisionMaxRange&quot;. Names that do not resolve are reported by Validate Profile and logged once at composition time rather than failing silently.</p></div>
<div class="set-list"><div class="set" id="f-apsprofile-override-property" data-search="Property" data-text="Exact name of the profile property to change, e.g. &quot;VisionMaxRange&quot;."><div class="set-head"><b>Property</b><span class="pin name"><i></i><small>Name</small></span></div><div class="set-facts"></div><div class="set-doc"><p>Exact name of the profile property to change, e.g. &quot;VisionMaxRange&quot;.</p></div></div><div class="set" id="f-apsprofile-override-number" data-search="Number" data-text="Value for numeric properties - float, int32, byte and enum."><div class="set-head"><b>Number</b><span class="pin float"><i></i><small>Float</small></span></div><div class="set-facts"><span>Default <b>0</b></span></div><div class="set-doc"><p>Value for numeric properties - float, int32, byte and enum.</p></div></div><div class="set" id="f-apsprofile-override-flag" data-search="Flag" data-text="Value for bool properties. Ignored when the named property is numeric."><div class="set-head"><b>Flag</b><span class="pin bool"><i></i><small>Boolean</small></span></div><div class="set-facts"><span>Default <b>Off</b></span></div><div class="set-doc"><p>Value for bool properties. Ignored when the named property is numeric.</p></div></div></div>

### APSSense Sample
<div class="comp-doc"><p>One sense&#x27;s contribution, flattened for a policy to reason about.</p><p>Deliberately small. A policy is called once per target per tick, so this is copied often; passing the full belief record would move roughly thirty times as much memory for data fusion does not use.</p></div>
<div class="set-list"><div class="set" id="f-apssense-sample-sense-id" data-search="Sense ID" data-text="&quot;Vision&quot;, &quot;Hearing&quot;, or whatever a custom sense returns from Get Sense ID."><div class="set-head"><b>Sense ID</b><span class="pin name"><i></i><small>Name</small></span></div><div class="set-facts"><span>Default <b>empty</b></span></div><div class="set-doc"><p>&quot;Vision&quot;, &quot;Hearing&quot;, or whatever a custom sense returns from Get Sense ID.</p></div></div><div class="set" id="f-apssense-sample-confidence" data-search="Confidence" data-text="What this sense reported, before weighting."><div class="set-head"><b>Confidence</b><span class="pin float"><i></i><small>Float</small></span></div><div class="set-facts"><span>Default <b>0</b></span></div><div class="set-doc"><p>What this sense reported, before weighting.</p></div></div><div class="set" id="f-apssense-sample-weight" data-search="Weight" data-text="The profile&#x27;s weight for this sense."><div class="set-head"><b>Weight</b><span class="pin float"><i></i><small>Float</small></span></div><div class="set-facts"><span>Default <b>1</b></span></div><div class="set-doc"><p>The profile&#x27;s weight for this sense.</p></div></div><div class="set" id="f-apssense-sample-is-active" data-search="Is Active" data-text="False when the sense is silent — it should contribute nothing."><div class="set-head"><b>Is Active</b><span class="pin bool"><i></i><small>Boolean</small></span></div><div class="set-facts"><span>Default <b>Off</b></span></div><div class="set-doc"><p>False when the sense is silent — it should contribute nothing.</p></div></div></div>

### APSTrait
<div class="comp-doc"><p>One observable fact about someone.</p><p>Identity in the perception kernel is pointer equality — the AI either knows an actor or it does not, and no disguise can change that. Traits are the layer that makes identity something you can be partly right about: an observer collects what it could actually make out, and matching that against known people is a separate, fallible step.</p><p>Observability is what makes recognition progressive. A coat colour reads across a courtyard; a face does not. Setting it honestly is what produces &quot;a person in a red coat&quot; at distance and &quot;that is Marcus&quot; up close, from the same data.</p></div>
<div class="set-list"><div class="set" id="f-apstrait-key" data-search="Key" data-text="What kind of fact this is — &quot;Clothing&quot;, &quot;Vehicle&quot;, &quot;Build&quot;, &quot;Voice&quot;, &quot;Face&quot;."><div class="set-head"><b>Key</b><span class="pin name"><i></i><small>Name</small></span></div><div class="set-facts"><span>Default <b>empty</b></span></div><div class="set-doc"><p>What kind of fact this is — &quot;Clothing&quot;, &quot;Vehicle&quot;, &quot;Build&quot;, &quot;Voice&quot;, &quot;Face&quot;.</p></div></div><div class="set" id="f-apstrait-value" data-search="Value" data-text="The value for this observer to match on — &quot;RedCoat&quot;, &quot;BlueSedan&quot;, &quot;Tall&quot;."><div class="set-head"><b>Value</b><span class="pin name"><i></i><small>Name</small></span></div><div class="set-facts"><span>Default <b>empty</b></span></div><div class="set-doc"><p>The value for this observer to match on — &quot;RedCoat&quot;, &quot;BlueSedan&quot;, &quot;Tall&quot;.</p></div></div><div class="set" id="f-apstrait-observability" data-search="Observability" data-text="How easily this is noticed [0..1]. 1 is unmissable at any range a target can be seen at; 0.1 needs a close, clear look. Suggested: clothing colour 0.9, build 0.8, vehicle 0.85, gait 0.4, face 0.25, voice 0.3 (and only when in earshot)."><div class="set-head"><b>Observability</b><span class="pin float"><i></i><small>Float</small></span></div><div class="set-facts"><span>Default <b>0.8</b></span><span>0 to 1</span></div><div class="set-doc"><p>How easily this is noticed [0..1]. 1 is unmissable at any range a target can be seen at; 0.1 needs a close, clear look.</p><p>Suggested: clothing colour 0.9, build 0.8, vehicle 0.85, gait 0.4, face 0.25, voice 0.3 (and only when in earshot).</p></div></div></div>

### APSView Fan

Each rim point is where sight stops along its direction: at a wall, past glass as far as vision gets through, at full range in the open. So the shape is what the AI can see, not just its settings.</p></div>

### APSView Point
<div class="comp-doc"><p>One of vision&#x27;s sample points on a target.</p></div>

### APSVisibility Sample
<div class="comp-doc"><p>One ray sample against a target, used for percentage-exposed visibility. Resolved from a mesh socket when available, otherwise from a local-space offset.</p></div>
<div class="set-list"><div class="set" id="f-apsvisibility-sample-socket-name" data-search="Socket Name" data-text="Mesh socket / bone to trace against. None = use Offset instead."><div class="set-head"><b>Socket Name</b><span class="pin name"><i></i><small>Name</small></span></div><div class="set-facts"><span>Default <b>empty</b></span></div><div class="set-doc"><p>Mesh socket / bone to trace against. None = use Offset instead.</p></div></div><div class="set" id="f-apsvisibility-sample-offset" data-search="Offset" data-text="Local-space fallback offset from the actor root (cm), used when SocketName is None or the socket does not exist. ### Perception Episode
<div class="comp-doc"><p>A record of one past engagement with a specific target. Written when target goes Lost from Detected or Tracked. Stored in FBeliefRecord.Episodes (ring buffer, max APS_MAX_EPISODES).</p><p>USAGE IN BEHAVIOR TREES: PerceptionCore → GetRecentEpisodes(Target) → Array of FPerceptionEpisode Then query: How was target lost last time? Where? How long was the engagement? Example: Last 3 losses were all Occluded at similar positions → bias search there.</p></div>
<div class="set-list"><div class="set" id="f-perception-episode-how-lost" data-search="How Lost" data-text="How this engagement ended."><div class="set-head"><b>How Lost</b><span class="pin enum"><i></i><small>Loss Reason</small></span></div><div class="set-facts"><span>Default <b>Unknown</b></span></div><div class="set-doc"><p>How this engagement ended.</p></div></div><div class="set" id="f-perception-episode-state-when-lost" data-search="State when Lost" data-text="State before going Lost (was AI Tracked or just Detected?)."><div class="set-head"><b>State when Lost</b><span class="pin enum"><i></i><small>Belief Lifecycle State</small></span></div><div class="set-facts"><span>Default <b>Undetected</b></span></div><div class="set-doc"><p>State before going Lost (was AI Tracked or just Detected?).</p></div></div><div class="set" id="f-perception-episode-location-when-lost" data-search="Location when Lost" data-text="World position of target when AI lost them."><div class="set-head"><b>Location when Lost</b><span class="pin vector"><i></i><small>Vector</small></span></div><div class="set-facts"><span>Default <b>(0, 0, 0)</b></span></div><div class="set-doc"><p>World position of target when AI lost them.</p></div></div><div class="set" id="f-perception-episode-aicamera-direction" data-search="AICamera Direction" data-text="Direction AI was facing when they lost the target. Useful for predicting blind spots."><div class="set-head"><b>AICamera Direction</b><span class="pin vector"><i></i><small>Vector</small></span></div><div class="set-facts"><span>Default <b>(1, 0, 0)</b></span></div><div class="set-doc"><p>Direction AI was facing when they lost the target. Senses run on their own intervals — vision every 0.15 s against a 0.05 s core tick — so on most ticks a sense has simply not been re-evaluated yet. That is not the same as reporting nothing, and belief must not decay while waiting for the nex"><div class="set-head"><b>Was Active Last Eval</b><span class="pin bool"><i></i><small>Boolean</small></span></div><div class="set-facts"><span>Default <b>Off</b></span></div><div class="set-doc"><p>What this sense said the last time it was actually asked.</p><p>Senses run on their own intervals — vision every 0.15 s against a 0.05 s core tick — so on most ticks a sense has simply not been re-evaluated yet. That is not the same as reporting nothing, and belief must not decay while waiting for the next evaluation. bIsActive still goes false in the gap, so the loss grace timer is unaffected; this is what tells the memory engine to hold rather than fade.</p></div></div></div>

Brief cover (thin pillar, doorframe) won&#x27;t immediately drop the target.</p><p>Defaults per sense: Vision       0.3s  — hide behind wall, gone fast Hearing      3.0s  — sound echo lingers Touch        0.5s  — lost contact Smell        20.0s — scent cloud persists Vibration    0.0s  — movement stopped, instant Damage       8.0s  — AI remembers being hit Echolocation 0.6s  — sonar pulse missed</p></div></div><div class="set" id="f-sense-loss-config-direct-cut" data-search="Direct Cut" data-text="If true, AI jumps directly to Lost once grace expires. ## Console commands
Type these in the console ([[`]] while playing, or the editor's **Cmd** box).

### aps.Visualizer
What the APS Visualizer shows. 0: nothing. 1 (default): everything. 2: status only (each AI's state over its head). (default `1`)

### aps.VisualizerPage
The page the APS Visualizer's screen panel shows (0 Senses, 1 Memory, 2 Brain, 3 Squad, 4 Events, 5 Player Model, 6 Environment). (default `0`)

### aps.UseSpatialIndex
1 (default): find perception candidates through the APS subsystem's spatial index. 0: fall back to scanning every Pawn in the world, once per agent, per gather. (default `1`)

### aps.Tune
aps.Tune <PropertyName> <Value> — set a profile value on every running agent, without touching the asset. Try: aps.Tune VisionMaxRange 5000
